Shortcut formula for C_sigma(n)

Source: R/sdf_shortcut.R
c_sigma_shortcut.Rd

Closed-form shortcut formula for the exact c_sigma. The form differs by scenario for a structural reason. Under S2 and S3 \(n\,C^2_\sigma(n)\) has the finite limit \(h\) (Theorem 1 of Wu, Shi and Tong, 2026), so the formula is \(A/\sqrt{n + \dots}\) with \(A = \sqrt{h}\) rounded to four decimals. Under S3 the minimum and maximum add precision of order \((\log n)^2\), against order \(n\) from the quartiles, which the terms \(c_1(\log n)^2 + c_2\log n\) stand for. Under S1 the range-based factor has no such limit and decays only like \(1/\log n\), so the formula is the logarithmic \(c_1/(\log n + c_2)^{c_3}\). Two constant sets are carried: version = "blue" (the default) for the factor of the BLUE of \(\sigma\), and version = "wan_luo_shi" for the factor of the SD estimators of Wan (under S1 and S2) and Shi (under S3). Both are fitted by minimax relative error over the paper's 39-point grid of \(n = 4Q+1\) (every such \(n\) from 5 to 101 and 14 larger ones up to 1001), with the constants exactly as the paper prints them.

Usage

c_sigma_shortcut(
  n,
  scenario = c("S3", "S1", "S2"),
  version = c("blue", "wan_luo_shi")
)

Arguments

n

Integer sample size(s); vectorized. Applied at any \(n\), as the source papers apply their formulas. No upper bound on \(n\) is checked; see Details for the accuracy beyond the grid.

scenario

One of "S1", "S2", "S3".

version

"blue" (default) or "wan_luo_shi".

Value

Numeric vector of approximate \(C_\sigma(n)\) values.

Details

Accuracy is the relative error of the printed constants against the exact factor, on the grid and at \(n = 2001, 5001, 10001\) beyond it. BLUE:

  • S1: \(0.8278/(\log n + 0.330)^{1.2041}\); error \(\le 0.37\%\) on the grid, and \(-0.8\%\), \(-1.4\%\), \(-1.9\%\) at \(n = 2001, 5001, 10001\): this formula has no limit to hold it, and its error grows slowly beyond the grid.

  • S2: \(1.1664/\sqrt{n - 0.863}\); error \(\le 0.13\%\) on the grid and \(\le 0.003\%\) beyond.

  • S3: \(1.1664/\sqrt{n + 5.267(\log n)^2 - 10.364\log n + 8.327}\); error \(\le 0.42\%\) on the grid and \(\le 0.32\%\) beyond.

Shortcut version:

  • S1: \(0.8705/(\log n + 0.418)^{1.2199}\); error \(\le 0.37\%\) on the grid, and \(-0.8\%\), \(-1.5\%\), \(-2.0\%\) beyond.

  • S2: \(1.1664/\sqrt{n - 0.845}\); error \(\le 0.099\%\) on the grid and \(\le 0.002\%\) beyond.

  • S3: \(1.1664/\sqrt{n + 5.191(\log n)^2 - 10.204\log n + 8.525}\); error \(\le 0.44\%\) on the grid and \(\le 0.27\%\) beyond.

Assumptions: iid normal data. The errors are measured on the grid of \(n = 4Q+1\), where the quartiles are single order statistics (type 7), and at the three larger sizes named; they are not bounds for every \(n\). c_sigma computes the exact factor at any \(n\) and definition.

References

Wu Z, Shi J, Tong T (2026). Precision of the imputed mean and standard deviation from a five-number summary. Manuscript.

Examples

c_sigma_shortcut(25, "S2")
#> [1] 0.2374137
c_sigma_shortcut(5000, "S3")    # no upper limit on n
#> [1] 0.01601851
